claims.statement: In March 2026 UOKiK described household OZE installations as investments costing tens of thousands of PLN and reported enforcement against hidden or unfair contract terms in the sector.

The Clean Air payment process uses completion documents including an installer acceptance protocol, showing that a document-defined completion event already exists in an important Polish renovation flow.

contrary_evidence: Many established installers already use deposits, staged invoices, bank finance, and ordinary acceptance protocols without a separate platform.
UOKiK enforcement demonstrates contract risk but does not establish that customers or installers will adopt third-party release control.

economics.acquisition_route: A low-cost local pilot, case studies with compliant installers, and channel sales through wholesalers and renovation-credit intermediaries
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-7 year path would require roughly 6,000 annual projects at about 850 PLN net platform revenue each, adjacent lender or insurer revenue, positive contribution margins, and retained founder ownership; reaching those volumes is unproven
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-16 hours per week for the initial Polish pilot, with contract review and inspections performed by paid specialists
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software and evidence-processing revenue less payment-partner, identity, signature, and verifier costs; customer money remains with a regulated partner
economics.payback: An installer may recover the fee if improved trust converts one additional project or if the record prevents one material payment dispute; this must be measured in a controlled pilot
economics.pricing: Target 0.8-1.2% of protected contract value, minimum 600 PLN per project, plus optional 99-199 PLN independent review fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installers repeat on every eligible contract; lenders and insurers could standardise the receipt across portfolios

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing dataset of milestone definitions, evidence failure modes, installer completion reliability, and verifier performance could improve exception routing and make the trust receipt more useful to lenders and insurers
fingerprint.customer: Reputable Polish residential OZE and thermomodernisation installers, with homeowners and renovation lenders as protected counterparties
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through the founder's family renewable-installation company, then distribute through equipment wholesalers, installer software vendors, credit brokers, and insurer partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Contract templates, evidence capture, independent exception review, and payment-release instructions; charge about 0.8-1.2% of protected contract value with a minimum project fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer or finance partner pays a platform fee when a protected project is opened and a smaller event fee whenever the licensed partner releases a verified milestone payment
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A high-value home project requires deposits or staged payments while the customer cannot independently verify completion and both sides fear delay, scope, or acceptance disputes

founder_fit: The family installation company offers a lawful, low-cost setting for testing milestone definitions without cold-start mass outreach
Evidence classification, anomaly detection, and workflow automation fit the founder's data-science and AI skills
A software-first pilot can run alongside employment and avoids a public-facing creator model
risks: Poorly drafted milestones could move rather than reduce disputes
Any appearance of unlicensed custody or payment initiation would create regulatory exposure
Installers with weak practices may seek the badge while resisting genuine verification
Independent review costs could erase margin on small jobs

structure.commercial_archetype: Transaction-fee milestone payment orchestration platform sold through installers and renovation finance partners
structure.control_point: The release instruction that binds a specific contract payment to a signed audit, evidence packet, acceptance protocol, or commissioning event
structure.critical_dependency: A licensed payment or escrow partner plus milestone language that is enforceable and verifiable without the platform itself taking custody

thesis: A white-label payment-assurance layer for Polish residential photovoltaic, heat-pump, and thermal-renovation contracts could let a licensed payment partner safeguard customer funds and release them only after contract-specific events such as the pre-installation audit, equipment delivery, signed acceptance protocol, and commissioning. Reputable installers could pay for a trust and conversion tool while homeowners receive a legible record of what unlocked each payment.
title: OZE Milestone Vault
uncertainties: Whether high-quality installers will pay rather than rely on staged invoices and reputation
Which Polish regulated partners will support conditional release at viable unit economics
Whether homeowners value safeguarded milestones enough to improve installer conversion
How frequently objective evidence can resolve acceptance without a physical expert visit
